source: docs/specs/05_focus_trees/major/worshipdom.md (the 'public / after reveal' columns of the branch tables) and docs/specs/04_mechanics/afrit_hidden_council.md, text secrecy rule 2. A two-face focus calls the scripted localisations zin_wsd_<key>_name and zin_wsd_<key>_desc, which read the public face while zin_afrit_revealed is unset and the true face after it. The public faces and descriptions never name the secret. The word 'Chancellor' in a public name is written 'Seal-Keeper' (banned-word list, class modern society).

focuses.publicDesc: The pilgrims' couriers carry letters, grain-prices and blessings between every court in Erdae. The hermitage gives them a chapter of their own.
focuses.trueDesc: Every courier is a pair of ears. The Seat of Whispers weaves them into one net that reaches every court.

focuses.publicDesc: The Leren court is proud and the harbour is busy. A few pilgrims and a letter of greeting will make the hermitage welcome there.
focuses.trueDesc: A listener at the Leren court hears what the sea-kings say of Parim and of the Treaty, and writes it down.

focuses.publicDesc: The wardens of Mirolon keep a lonely road. Pilgrims bring them bread and the news from the north.
focuses.trueDesc: The pilgrims on the Mirolon road count the banners of the south, and carry the count home.

focuses.publicDesc: The caravan roads of the East are long, and the sick along them are many. A chapter of the hermitage will tend them.
focuses.trueDesc: The East will be the reserve seat. The Eastern Branch opens houses at every court that might one day kneel.

focuses.publicDesc: Merchants talk, and the pilgrims listen kindly. What the traders say of the western ports is worth a prayer.
focuses.trueDesc: Gossip from the western ports tells the hermitage who has sailed north, and why.

focuses.publicDesc: Some troubles cannot be mended by bread. The Hands of Mercy go quietly where a quiet word is needed.
focuses.trueDesc: A voice that is raised against the Faithful is raised no more. The Silent Knives do their work without a name.

focuses.publicDesc: Where a road runs, a pilgrim walks it. The hermitage will have no road in Erdae without one.
focuses.trueDesc: Every road has a pilgrim on it, and every pilgrim a tongue. Nothing is said in Erdae that the hermitage does not hear.

focuses.publicDesc: The pilgrims' houses are linked by messengers, so that no pilgrim in need goes unheard.
focuses.trueDesc: The net is whole. News of the Lands of the Sun now reaches the hermitage before it reaches the sun's own kings.

focuses.publicDesc: The temples have many friends at the Golden Court, and the court has found the temples useful. A chair is kept for them.
focuses.trueDesc: The Seat of Seals holds Aenor's offices through men who owe the hermitage their places. Merovan is the first of them.

focuses.publicDesc: The Keeper of the King's Seals is an honest and weary man. The temples send him counsel, and he is grateful.
focuses.trueDesc: Merovan keeps the seals of Aenor and the will of the hermitage. He signs what the hermitage drafts.

focuses.publicDesc: The Golden Court sells its offices. A pious house that buys them will fill them with honest men.
focuses.trueDesc: The King sells his offices, and the hermitage buys them. Every seat that is bought is a seat the Council cannot lose.

focuses.publicDesc: The temples pray for the King's long life. A special office is said for him in every house of the First Light.
focuses.trueDesc: The Council decided in 4A 1746 that the King is a liability. The verdict is read again, and the instrument must be chosen.

focuses.publicDesc: The Golden King loves a rich gift. The temples send him the best of their harvests and their craftsmen.
focuses.trueDesc: A king who is fed and flattered watches nothing. The more he takes, the less he asks where it came from.

focuses.publicDesc: The King's league against the dark deserves every blessing. The temples offer its banners shelter and its captains a hearth.
focuses.trueDesc: A league that gathers captains and scholars may begin to ask questions. The Council will know every one of them.

focuses.publicDesc: A vigil is kept for the King's health, in the palace chapel and in every house of the First Light.
focuses.trueDesc: The King will leave this world at the Council's hour. The instrument must be chosen, and its price paid.

focuses.publicDesc: Not every hour needs a deed. The temples pray for patience and leave the King to his reign.
focuses.trueDesc: The Council holds its hand. The King lives on, and the Council rules behind him.

focuses.publicDesc: The lords of the Concord have grievances. The temples sit with them and listen.
focuses.trueDesc: A dominion that curses the Golden King's tithe is a dominion that will not mourn him.

focuses.publicDesc: The temples bless the Golden King and wish him a hundred years upon the throne.
focuses.trueDesc: A living king is the best of cloaks. The Council keeps him in his chair and rules through his seals.

focuses.publicDesc: The houses of the First Light send their best physicians to the palace. The King will want for no remedy.
focuses.trueDesc: A physician of the Houses stands at the King's bed. What he gives the King is the Council's to choose.

focuses.public: A Steady Hand on the Seals
focuses.publicDesc: The seals of the realm should be in steady hands. The temples lend their scribes and their patience.
focuses.trueDesc: On the night, the seals must be in the Council's hands and no other's. Every scribe is placed.

focuses.publicDesc: The temples bless the King's table, and send priests to say grace over every dish.
focuses.trueDesc: The King's tasters see too much. They are persuaded to look elsewhere, or not to look at all.

focuses.publicDesc: The choirs of the temples learn new hymns for a crown that will one day pass.
focuses.trueDesc: When the King dies, every temple must be ready to name the Deliverer on the same morning.

focuses.publicDesc: The Mistfall feast is the King's favourite. The temples keep a vigil through it, and pray for the realm.
focuses.trueDesc: The night is chosen. After the Mistfall feast the Golden King will not wake.

focuses.publicDesc: When a reign ends, the seals pass to those who keep them best. The temples are ready to be those keepers.
focuses.trueDesc: The Council commits itself. The Deliverer will take the crown of Aenor, and the seals will be laid before him.

focuses.publicDesc: A young prince of an old line needs a patient tutor. The temples offer the best they have.
focuses.trueDesc: A crown on a child's head and a hand on the child's shoulder. The Council rules and the child reigns.

focuses.publicDesc: The priests who keep the great censers of Parim and Zilin form a chapter of their own, to order the hymns and the feasts.
focuses.trueDesc: The Seat of Censers is the Council's public face: the temples, the hymns and the miracles that make a god beloved.

focuses.publicDesc: The old rolls of the royal lines should be kept and copied. The temples endow chairs for the scholars who keep them.
focuses.trueDesc: Scholars who ask where the Deliverer's line begins are given chairs and pensions, and teach something else.

focuses.publicDesc: The Deliverer is shown to the people in light and in song. The people love what they see.
focuses.trueDesc: The face the people love is a veil. Beneath it the Council's work goes on, and every loss to the secret is halved.

focuses.true: A God for an Empty Throne
focuses.publicDesc: When a king dies, the people look for someone to hold the crown. The Deliverer has guarded Aenor since the fall of Elzon, and will guard it still.
focuses.trueDesc: The proclamation is ready. When the throne is empty the temples will cry the Deliverer's name before any other can be heard.

focuses.publicDesc: The hermitage keeps old relics in a deep vault. A chapter of scholars is set to guard and catalogue them.
focuses.trueDesc: The Seat of Relics holds the artifacts of the Council: the Necklace and the three lesser works.

focuses.publicDesc: A strange old guest has come to the Reliquary, and the scholars give him a room. He is courteous, and he has been there longer than anyone can say.
focuses.trueDesc: Sevrin took the Necklace once and was given unending life. He serves the Seat of Relics, and he does not forget.

focuses.publicDesc: The masons of the hermitage open new doors in the old walls, so that pilgrims may come and go in winter.
focuses.trueDesc: The Ring of Doors answers to those who know its measures. The Reliquary teaches them.

focuses.publicDesc: Great vows are written in gold on the walls of the temple, so that none may say they were forgotten.
focuses.trueDesc: The Crown of Witnesses draws strength from sworn oaths. Every oath in gold is a coin in its treasury.

focuses.true: Attune the Bracelet of the First Seal
focuses.publicDesc: The oldest seal of the hermitage is brought out and shown to the pilgrims at the turn of the year.
focuses.trueDesc: The Bracelet of the First Seal guards its wearer. The Reliquary wakes its power one ward at a time.

focuses.publicDesc: The deep vault of the hermitage is lit at last, and the scholars go down with lamps to read the oldest rolls.
focuses.trueDesc: The Necklace of the Abyss is brought to its full waking. The Necklace is strongest in the prepared heart of the Middle Kingdom.

focuses.publicDesc: The pilgrims bring stories of a green light in the far north, in a castle on the ice. The scholars write the stories down.
focuses.trueDesc: The Council wants Glo. The green crystal in the castle of Yeldenne is the one prize it does not yet hold.

focuses.publicDesc: The pilgrim houses of the coast outfit ships for those who would go north in the spring.
focuses.trueDesc: The ships are ready and the crews sworn. They will sail when the Council gives the word.

focuses.publicDesc: Guides who know the northern ice are hired to lead the pilgrims safely over it.
focuses.trueDesc: The guides are hunters. When the stranger's ship comes ashore, they will be waiting on the cold beach.

focuses.publicDesc: Even the Deliverer must rest. The hermitage keeps its doors shut for a season, and the pilgrims wait outside, singing.
focuses.trueDesc: The wound is a weakness the world must not see. The hermitage hides it behind a season of rest.

focuses.publicDesc: The temples bless the new throne in Parim, and the crowned Deliverer receives the oaths of the realm.
focuses.trueDesc: Afrit sits in Parim as Aurevan, King of Aenor, First of His Name. The kingdom kneels to a god it does not know.

focuses.publicDesc: The royal host is blessed by the temples. Its captains swear before the altar to guard the kingdom.
focuses.trueDesc: Every captain has sworn to the Deliverer by name. The army of Aenor is now the Council's.

focuses.publicDesc: The new reign wants peace. The temples ask every rival to put down his claim and live quietly.
focuses.trueDesc: Rival claimants have a way of falling silent. What is done with those who do not is not written in any roll.

focuses.publicDesc: The crowned Deliverer receives the oaths of the Faithful in the great temple of Parim.
focuses.trueDesc: The oaths of the coronation feed the Crown of Witnesses. The kingdom swears, and the crown remembers.

focuses.publicDesc: The enemies of Aenor come from the west, the north and the south. The Deliverer vows that Parim shall not fall.
focuses.trueDesc: Afrit will not run. He holds Parim, and stakes the whole kingdom on the Necklace.

focuses.publicDesc: A wise regency keeps the realm in good order, and the realm is content.
focuses.trueDesc: The regency has no end. The throne is kept warm for a king who will never be crowned.

focuses.publicDesc: Envoys carry the Deliverer's greeting to every eastern court, and ask what the courts need.
focuses.trueDesc: The East is where the Deliverer will rule from. A second embassy asks those who refused to think again.

focuses.publicDesc: The kings of the East offer the Deliverer a crown of the dawn, and he accepts it for their sake.
focuses.trueDesc: The kings who knelt have named him King of the East. The Worshipdom is now the Dominion of the East.

focuses.publicDesc: The doubtful courts of the East are sent patient letters, and promised that the door stays open.
focuses.trueDesc: A king who refused the King of the East has chosen his war. The Dominion marks the one with the most land.

focuses.publicDesc: Great numbers of pilgrims come up the caravan roads to see the Deliverer, and are fed at the hermitage.
focuses.trueDesc: The caravan kings send men with their pilgrimage. Each court that knelt owes the Dominion its levy.

focuses.publicDesc: The Deliverer sits in council with the kings of the East, to plan the care of the roads.
focuses.trueDesc: Afrit takes the field himself. In the war council he is a marshal, and his captains learn what the Necklace has made of him.

focuses.publicDesc: The Faithful of the East gather at the hermitage in great number, to sing and to be fed.
focuses.trueDesc: The Host of the East is raised: the levies of every court that knelt, under the banner of the Dominion.

focuses.publicDesc: The pilgrims ask leave to walk through the woods of the elves on their way to the west.
focuses.trueDesc: The elves refused, and a refusal is a war. The Host of the East turns toward the Magical Forest.

focuses.publicDesc: The pilgrims who went east turn homeward, and the road to Parim fills with song.
focuses.trueDesc: The Host marches west. The King of the East is coming for the Crown of Aen and for his brother.

focuses.publicDesc: The pilgrims and the royal host meet on the field before Parim, and the song of the Faithful is heard above the camps.
focuses.trueDesc: Afrit stands before his brother's host. The war for Parim is the war of two sons of Ein.

focuses.publicDesc: The Deliverer shows himself to the people in the fullness of his glory.
focuses.trueDesc: The mask is thrown off. The Deliverer is Afrit, and he asks the world to bow before him as he is.

focuses.publicDesc: The Faithful gather in the open to sing, in every land where a house of the First Light stands.
focuses.trueDesc: In every land where the Houses stand, the Faithful rise at the Deliverer's word, to take their court from within.

focuses.publicDesc: The people stand in awe of the Deliverer and give him their worship freely.
focuses.trueDesc: Worship that is not freely given is fear. The Dominion governs by both, and the two are hard to tell apart.

focuses.publicDesc: The hermitage is guarded by wardens whom no pilgrim has ever seen.
focuses.trueDesc: The servants beyond the veil are called. What they are is answered only by what they do.

focuses.publicDesc: Each house of the First Light is made a refuge, with walls against the storm and doors against the cold.
focuses.trueDesc: A house that is purged is not lost. Its walls hold, its stores are hidden, and the Faithful inside wait.

focuses.publicDesc: The light of the Deliverer falls on every land, and every land is glad of it.
focuses.trueDesc: Afrit proclaims kingship over all Erdae, larger than the lands he holds. Parim is his seat once more.

focuses.publicDesc: The Houses of the First Light are restored in every land, and their doors are open to all.
focuses.trueDesc: The old Council sits again, and every court in Erdae has a seat in it that it did not choose.

focuses.publicDesc: The throne of the Deliverer is raised in Parim, and the world is called to see it.
focuses.trueDesc: Afrit rules through worship, bargains, corruption and every captured house. The throne is ash, and so is the age it sits on.
